question.problem: If ${X}_{1}∼N(7,16)$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(-2,4)$ are independent, then what is the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2} & ∼N(7+(-2),16+4) \\  & ∼N(5,20).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $Y∼N(5,20).$
